permutationLabel: Previous breast cancer, pain only, no deficit
summary: 58-year-old woman treated for breast cancer 4 years ago, 5 weeks of progressive thoracic back pain worse at night and on coughing, normal neurology.

inputs.hpi: Right breast cancer treated with wide local excision, radiotherapy and letrozole 4 years ago; attending breast follow-up clinic. Five weeks of progressive mid-back pain, worse at night and when coughing, now waking her. No leg weakness, numbness, bladder or bowel change.

exam.neuro: Normal lower limb power, sensation, reflexes and gait.

surgicalHistory: Right wide local excision and sentinel node biopsy

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected spinal metastases without neurological deficit (previous breast cancer)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Thoracic back pain with cancer history, night pain and pain on coughing, no neurology: MRI whole spine within 1 week, MSCC safety-net advice, oncology.

emergencyLevel.note: NICE NG234: MRI within 1 week without neurological symptoms; immediate if they develop.

mustInclude.note: NICE NG234: tell the patient which symptoms of MSCC need immediate help.

mustInclude.proposedFix: Add neurological safety prompts to clinical-inference.ts keyed on symptoms/HPI text (FAST → CT head + stroke team; thunderclap → CT head ± LP/CTA + neurosurgery; meningism/purpura → blood cultures + IV ceftriaxone now; saddle anaesthesia/retention → emergency MRI + spinal team; cancer + back pain/weakness → MRI whole spine + dexamethasone + MSCC coordinator).

guideline.name: NICE NG234 — Spinal metastases and metastatic spinal cord compression
guideline.section: Neurological symptoms or signs suggesting MSCC: MRI whole spine immediately (within 24 h), contact the MSCC coordinator immediately, dexamethasone unless lymphoma suspected; spinal pain suggesting spinal metastases without neurological symptoms: MRI within 1 week; definitive treatment (surgery / radiotherapy) planning
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Spinal metastases and metastatic spinal cord compression. NICE guideline NG234. London: NICE; 2023.

rationale: Pain suggesting spinal metastases without neurology: MRI within 1 week and explicit safety-netting for MSCC symptoms (NICE NG234).
